This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.
2.

The petition averments briefly stated as under; That on 15.05.2023 at about 9.00 a.m. petitioner was crossing the road on B.B. Main Road, near Jakkur Aero Drum, Yelahanka, Bengaluru, at that time, a Bajaj SCCH-5 Pulsar Bike bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JT-6508 being ridden by its rider at a very high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, due to the said impact,
petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Prolife Multispeciality Hospital, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient and spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- for treatment, medicines, food and nourishment expenses.
3. At the time of the accident, petitioner was aged about 36 years, hale and healthy, working as Security Guard at Elite Company and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is not able to do his daily activities and cannot concentrate on his work and injuries caused are permanent in nature.

With regard to accident in crime No.180/2023 is registered against the SCCH-5 rider of the said Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle before the Yelahanka Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.

4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared through counsel and filed written statement and denied occurrence of the alleged accident involving the Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JT-3508 by its rider and the alleged accident was occurred due to carelessness on the petitioner himself.

Further respondent No.1 submitted that, said vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 vide its policy No.201250020118704135800000 valid from 20.09.2019 SCCH-5 to 20.09.2023 and the driver of the said vehicle was having valid driving licence at the time of accident.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied involvement of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JT-6508.

Further respondent No.2 denied injuries sustained by the petitioner, treatment taken by him and further submitted that, it has issued policy of insurance in respect of said motor cycle in favour of respondent No.1 and same was valid from 21.09.2018 to 20.09.2023 and its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further respondent No.1 also seeks protection under Sec.147 and 149 of M.V.Act.
Respondent No.2 submitted that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act SCCH-5 and compensation claimed by the petitioner is on higher side.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

: : ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 15.05.2023 at about 9.00 a.m. when the petitioner was a pedestrian on BB Road to go for security work, near Jakkuru Aero Drum,
Yelahanka, Bengaluru at that time, one motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JT-6508 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so how much and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
SCCH-5 7.
In order to prove the case, Petitioner herself examined as PW-1, examined Medical Record Officer of Prolife Multispeciality Hospital as PW-2 and marked 19 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19.
On the other hand, respondents have not adduced any evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record and my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove the case, petitioner examined himself as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts SCCH-5 averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated.

In order to prove road traffic accident PW-1 produced and marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint as Ex.P.2, copy of crime details form as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch as Ex.P.4, copy of AR Form as Ex.P.5,
copy of wound certificate as Ex.P.6, copy of charge sheet with statements as Ex.P.7, copy of reply as Ex.P.9.
10.
Further to substantiate the petitioner's case, petitioner has examined Medical Record Officer as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1, PW-2 and documents those have marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19 corroborates the case of the petitioner about occurrence of the road traffic accident dated 15.05.2023 as alleged in the petition.

11. Per contra, except filing of written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to Anil Alias Anil Kumar Mishra vs Raghu P on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90640810/
3 disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as SCCH-5 alleged in the petition and to discard the evidence of PW-1.

sentences.text:
Since in the absence of iota of evidence, this tribunal held that the petitioner sustained the injuries due to the accident occurred on 15.05.2023 at about 9.00 a.m.
when he was crossing the road on B.B. Main Road, near Jakkuru Aero Drum, Yelahanka, Bengaluru.
12.
It is evident from police papers that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of rider of Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JT-6508.
Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.

13. Issue No.2:- As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained left hand 2 nd metacarpal shaft fracture, left forearm distal 1/3rd both bone SCCH-5 fracture, right leg both bone fracture, for the said injuries, he took treatment in the form of surgery of left hand 2nd metacarpal ORIF + K wiring, left forearm both bone ORIF + plating and right tibia CRIF + IMILN.

To prove the said injuries and treatment taken by him, petitioner has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.6, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.10 issued by Prolife Multi Speciality Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 15.05.2023 to 27.05.2023 i.e., for a period of 12 days.

Further he has furnished medical bills for Rs.3,73,158/- marked as Ex.P.11, advance receipt as Ex.P.12 and medical prescriptions as Ex.P.13.
14.

In support of his case, Medical Record Officer of Prolife Multispeciality Hospital is examined as PW- 2 and got marked authorization letter as Ex.P.15, copy of SCCH-5 MLC Extract as Ex.P.16, copy of police intimation as Ex.P.17, case sheet as Ex.P.18 and X-ray Films as Ex.P.19.
Petitioner has not adduced the evidence of Doctor who treated him.

15. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 36 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.14, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 01.01.1987 and the alleged accident is occurred on 15.05.2023, accordingly relying on Ex.P.14 his age is considered about 37 years as on the date of accident.
16. As per the case of the petitioner, he was working as Security Guard at Elite Company, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.
SCCH-5 17
. It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.10, petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 15.05.2023 to 27.05.2023 at Prolife Multispeciality Hospital i.e., for 12 days
. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.11 medical bills for Rs.3,73,158/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is concerned.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.6 in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 15.05.2023.

So as per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained left eye swelling, left hand 2 nd metacarpal shaft fracture, left forearm distal 1/3rd both bone fracture, right leg both bone fracture, which are grievous in nature.

Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Raghunath P. for the SCCH-5 Anil Alias Anil Kumar Mishra vs Raghu P on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90640810/
4 offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

sentences.text:
So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
18.
Per contra except denial in the written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor to proved the allegations as alleged in the written statement.
In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case.

Considering the nature of the injuries sustained, treatment taken and medical expenses incurred by the petitioner,
he is entitled for global compensation of SCCH-5 Rs.6,50,000/- which includes medical bills of Rs.3,73,158/-.
19. Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,50,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

20. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JT-6508 which was valid from 21.09.2018 to 20.09.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 15.05.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that, respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of SCCH-5 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.

21. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.6,50,000/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Fifty Thousand Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept SCCH-5 in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
